metadata.direction_rule: Tractability is scored in the direction the signature wants, not in the direction the target class is usually drugged. AKT1, BCL2, CAMK2A, GPX4, SIRT1 and HMOX1 all have small-molecule precedent as inhibitors and all need to go UP in Alzheimer's, so they are scored as the harder, activation problem.
metadata.purpose: Per-target modality annotation for Alzheimer's disease. Tells the design layer which proteins a small molecule can realistically engage.

schema.small_molecule_tractability: 0-1 ordinal prior that a drug-like small molecule can productively engage this protein; 0 marks a transcriptional readout rather than a target
schema.note: the reason for the value, so it can be argued with

metadata.curation_rule: Ordinal priors reflecting precedent in the public literature, on the same scale as the MS and Parkinson's annotations. Judgements, not measurements.
metadata.readout_convention: A target scoring below 0.2 is treated by the design engine as a readout: the profile may require its expression to move, but no arm of a designed molecule will be assigned to bind it.
metadata.the_defining_problem: The two proteins that define the disease pathology are the two a small molecule reaches worst. Tau (MAPT) is intrinsically disordered and scores 0.15; APP is a substrate rather than an enzyme and scores 0.2, and amyloid-beta itself is a cleavage product with no transcript to score at all. Alzheimer's is therefore the hardest test of the tractability floor so far: the profile has to reach amyloid through BACE1, gamma-secretase and ADAM10, and tau through GSK3B, FYN and CDK5, exactly as the clinical field has tried to.

ABCA1.note: Lipid exporter; LXR agonism raises expression

ACHE.note: The most precedented target in the disease; three approved inhibitors

ADAM10.note: alpha-secretase; activation, not inhibition, is wanted, which is harder

AIF1.note: Iba1; the standard microglial activation marker

AKT1.note: Activation is the wanted direction and kinase precedent is almost entirely inhibitors; allosteric activators are tool compounds

APOE.note: The strongest common genetic risk factor and not a conventional pocket target; structure-corrector chemotypes are early

APP.note: Amyloid precursor; a substrate rather than an enzyme. Reached through its secretases or by translation inhibition, not by binding APP

ATP5F1A.note: ATP synthase subunit; a readout of mitochondrial function

BACE1.note: Aspartyl protease with extensive small-molecule precedent; four phase 2/3 programmes

BCL2.note: Venetoclax-class precedent is inhibition; raising anti-apoptotic BCL2 is the wanted direction and has no small-molecule route

BDNF.note: A growth factor; delivered or induced, not bound

C1QA.note: Complement initiator; antibody approaches, few small molecules

CAMK2A.note: CaMKII; inhibitors exist but activation is the wanted direction

CD33.note: Siglec; antibody and glycomimetic approaches, few small molecules

CDK5.note: Kinase; selectivity over CDK1/2 is the practical difficulty

CHAT.note: Choline acetyltransferase; activation is not a realistic small-molecule goal, treated as a readout of cholinergic neuron loss

CHRM1.note: M1 muscarinic receptor; xanomeline precedent, orthosteric selectivity is the historical obstacle

CHRNA4.note: Alpha-4 nicotinic subunit; allosteric modulation by galantamine

CHRNA7.note: Alpha-7 nicotinic receptor; agonists and PAMs reached phase 3

CSF1R.note: Receptor kinase with multiple inhibitors, several brain-penetrant

CX3CR1.note: Chemokine receptor on microglia; antagonists exist, agonism is the wanted direction

DLG4.note: PSD-95; a structural readout of synapse density

FYN.note: Src-family kinase; saracatinib repurposed against it

GFAP.note: Astrocyte activation marker and a plasma biomarker; a readout

GLP1R.note: Peptide agonists are approved; oral small molecules are emerging

GPX4.note: Selenoprotein; covalent inhibitors are known, activators are not, and activation is the wanted direction

GRIA1.note: AMPA subunit; positive modulators have precedent

GRIN1.note: Obligatory NMDA subunit; memantine is approved

GSK3B.note: Well-precedented kinase; tideglusib and lithium engage it

HMOX1.note: Heme oxygenase; an inducible compensatory response, raised by upstream Nrf2 activation rather than bound

IDE.note: Insulin-degrading enzyme; activators are unusual chemical matter

IL1B.note: A cytokine, reached through NLRP3 or receptor antagonists

IL6.note: A cytokine; readout of glial activation

INSR.note: Insulin receptor; activated by insulin, intranasal delivery is the route

MAPK14.note: p38 alpha; extensive inhibitor precedent, neflamapimod is brain-penetrant

MAPT.note: Tau is intrinsically disordered; reached by antibodies, antisense, or aggregation inhibitors rather than binding pockets

MME.note: Neprilysin, an abeta-degrading peptidase; activation is the goal and precedent is thin

NCSTN.note: gamma-secretase scaffold subunit; not directly targeted

NDUFS1.note: Complex I subunit; inhibitors are known, activators are not

NEFL.note: Neurofilament light, the neuronal-injury biomarker; a readout

NFKB1.note: Transcription factor; reached through upstream kinases

NTRK2.note: TrkB; agonist small molecules reported, none proven

PIN1.note: Prolyl isomerase; covalent and peptidomimetic inhibitors reported, activation unlikely

PPP2CA.note: Catalytic subunit of PP2A; activation is wanted and phosphatases are hard to activate

PRKAA1.note: AMPK; activators including metformin's indirect action

PSEN1.note: Catalytic subunit of gamma-secretase; inhibitors and modulators exist, but substrate promiscuity (Notch) limits use

RAB5A.note: Early-endosome GTPase; reached through p38 signalling

SIGMAR1.note: Sigma-1 receptor; several ligands including donepezil and blarcamesine

SIRT1.note: Deacetylase; activators are reported but their mechanism is disputed

SLC18A3.note: Vesicular acetylcholine transporter; imaging ligands exist, therapeutic modulators do not

SLC2A1.note: GLUT1; the glucose hypometabolism marker, activators unprecedented

SOD1.note: Antioxidant enzyme; activation is not a practical target

SOD2.note: Mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme; induced rather than bound

SORL1.note: Sorting receptor for APP; a retromer-linked trafficking readout

SYP.note: Synaptophysin; a synapse-loss marker, not a target

SYT1.note: Calcium sensor for vesicle fusion; a readout

TFEB.note: Master lysosomal regulator; activated through mTOR inhibition rather than directly

TNF.note: A cytokine; biologics dominate, small-molecule modulators are rare

TREM2.note: Microglial receptor; agonist antibodies are the modality, small molecules are early

TYROBP.note: DAP12 adaptor; signalling readout for TREM2
